lead.headline: Redlined 1930s neighborhoods hold 13.35 toxic-release plants per 100 square kilometers, six times the 2.21 in 'B' areas
lead.number: Toxic-release plants per 100 km²: D areas 13.35, C 5.82, B 2.21, A 0.07; D denser than B in 119 of 212 cities.
lead.watch_out: The plants likely came before the maps, and redlining-to-pollution research is already published.
